research_rationale:
Identity: Executive Order 13276 of November 15, 2002, Delegation of Responsibilities Concerning Undocumented Aliens Interdicted or Intercepted in the Caribbean Region (67 FR 69985, November 19, 2002; FR Doc. 02-29580), read in full from the official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13276.txt (own-text boundary verified for the whole order). It rests on sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) of the Immigration and Nationality Act and 3 U.S.C. 301. Fourteen machine clauses cover it: the recital; section 1 lead-in; 1(a)(i) and 1(a)(ii) (Attorney General custody, facilities and screening); 1(b) (Secretary of State); 1(c)(i) and 1(c)(ii) (Secretary of Defense); section 2 (definition of mass migration); and section 3 (scope) with paragraphs (a) to (e). The inventory is confirmed without correction. Later instrument: Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (68 FR 10619, March 5, 2003), section 1, amends Executive Order 13276 by striking The Attorney General and the Attorney General wherever they appear in section 1 and inserting the Secretary of Homeland Security; its section 92 provides that it becomes effective on March 1, 2003, so that date is used rather than the signing date. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the affected clauses continue, amended, with the Secretary of Homeland Security as actor in place of the Attorney General. The words appear in 1(a)(i), 1(a)(ii), 1(b), 1(c)(i) and 1(c)(ii); the section 1 lead-in, the recital and sections 2 and 3 name no Attorney General and are unchanged. The dossier's chain entry attributing a 1995 date to Executive Order 12977 for this amendment is a mislabelled copy of the Executive Order 13286 text and is not used. Ending search: the order has no sunset, duration or terminating condition. The held corpus was searched for the number 13276: the only instrument that acts on it is Executive Order 13286. Presidential memoranda published at 82 FR 48875 (2017) and 90 FR 38913 (August 12, 2025) each state that the memorandum does not affect Executive Order 12807 or Executive Order 13276, which shows the order treated as in force in 2025 and is not an amendment or ending. Executive Order 12807 is cited in sections 1(c)(ii) and 3(a) of this order as a separate order and is not held as revoked. Current predicate: the U.S. Code note under 8 U.S.C. 1182 (release point 119-121, in the packet) prints the order as amended by Executive Order 13286 section 1 with the Secretary of Homeland Security in place of the Attorney General; 32 CFR 245.9 (eCFR, amended through 2026-08-17, in the packet as CURRENT:EO:13276#1) lists it among authorities; the statutes it cites (8 U.S.C. 1182(f), 8 U.S.C. 1185(a)(1) and 3 U.S.C. 301) remain in the Code. Bounded searches read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML; one hit, 32 CFR 245.9) and later-events:ofr_catalog (two hits, both Executive Order 13286). Limit disclosed: the 2025 memorandum is a recital, not a source for how any clause was applied after 2003; the claim rests on the absence of any ending instrument and the order's indefinite term.
